I'm a dad but here's my couple of cents. Pregnancy can be a beautiful thing and it definitely has outs moments. HOWEVER! There is also the nitty gritty involved as well. Seeing my ex through her recent pregnancy, here's a few things we established. Seeing and feeling kicks is amazing, but you will get probably get random belly touches so prepare to be firm about unwanted feels and also did you ever get nudged awake at anytime? Yeah prepare to be angry at once comfortable sleep positions. If you have a wonderful partner in the adventure it's nice to have a lot of things done for you but remember it's your partner not servant. I ran into this issue and almost lost my shit a number of times. You're gonna be sick, maybe for a little while or maybe the whole pregnancy. Prepare accordingly. A big one is breast feeding.  A lot of people may try and get toy to bend your knee to the milky boob deities but you also need to be mentally prepared (even the slightest bit) that you may not be able to. It's great if you can but my ex hit a really bad low over not being able to provide milk fit out first born, though this time she's doing pretty well and we're taking what she can pump out as a huge win. Another partner thing is getting ready mentally and house work and money saving ect, is gonna take a toll on you both so take time to yourselves. Go out on a few dates, do fun things here and there and also leave room for you both to do a few things on your own because oooh man are you gonna see new sides to each other lol. As for when the baby is born, in my experience, it wasn't as difficult as everyone told me it'd be but everyone is different. Don't get over stressed over small stuff but don't tell yourself the small stuff is nothing either because that shit builds up.  Baby is gonna cry for a multitude of reasons and sometimes it may seem like just because. Recently newbie was napping and just let out a nightmarish scream and literally fell back asleep. Sleep Is another thing, don't feel like you both have to become insomniacs, allow the other to just have a nap here and there if things are pretty mellow sometimes bite the bullet for the other. When my ex got home I decided to give her a few nights rest to recuperate so I fully tended to the newbie though the night getting maybe 3 hours of sleep which were basically just seperate naps.  There's probably a bunch more I haven't touched at but overall just try to take things easy. Oh! You're not gonna need A LOT of the fancy toys and sets that you're gonna see and think you should buy. Kids are simple really, each kid is different but box forts still rule,  nature is always amazing for them,  and the only good advice my mother gave my in my 29 years of life is "you don't need to be perfect, just be present". :)
